name: Y is reached twice: by a long route first, by a short route later
note: Unit costs. Y can be reached as S–A–X–Y (depth 3) or S–B–Y (depth 2); the goal G hangs off Y, so the shortest path is S–B–Y–G (3 edges). Plain DFS dives S–A–X–Y–G and returns 4 edges; BFS returns S–B–Y–G. Depth-bounded DFS with bound 3 FAILS even though G is at depth 3: Y is closed at depth 3 (where it may not be expanded) and S–B–Y is then skipped because Y is already on CLOSED. DFID reopens Y when it is met again at depth 2, so its round with bound 3 finds S–B–Y–G.
